name: IRAQ

flag.title: Flag of Iraq
flag.note: Green, white & red with Kufic script

lead: Iraq lies in the Middle East, between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. People here invented writing and cities about 5,000 years ago. Baghdad, the capital, has nearly eight million people. Snowy mountains rise in the north. Hot desert fills the west.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The Tigris and Euphrates rivers flow south to the Persian Gulf. The flat, fertile land between them is Mesopotamia. Great cities were born here.
The west is pure desert. It bakes at over 50 °C. The far south has the Mesopotamian Marshes, a huge wetland of reeds. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
animals: Smooth-coated otters, water buffalo, and millions of migrating birds fill the southern marshes. The Basra reed warbler nests nowhere else on Earth. Striped hyenas roam the desert at night.
The giant Tigris catfish grows longer than a child is tall. Babylon's walls once showed the Asiatic lion. Sadly, it vanished in the 20th century.
culture: Sumerians pressed wedge shapes into clay here around 3200 BCE. That was the world's first writing. Iraqis still love poetry and read it aloud with family.
Dates are the national food, and Iraq grows over 1,000 kinds. Friday lunch is often lamb with saffron rice. Strong cardamom tea comes in tiny glass cups.
history: About 5,000 years ago, the Sumerians built the world's first cities. They also invented the wheel and schools. Babylon later became the greatest city on Earth.
Baghdad was founded in 762 CE and became the world's science hub. Scholars there invented algebra. Oil and wars shaped modern Iraq.
wows: The world's oldest story, Gilgamesh, was pressed into clay here over 4,000 years ago.
Babylonians invented the 60-minute hour and the 360-degree circle. We still use both.
Iraq has the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves, says OPEC.
Ancient Ur is believed to be the birthplace of the biblical Abraham.
Al-Khwarizmi of Baghdad invented algebra around 820 CE, and the word is Arabic.
Reflooded after 2003, the southern marshes earned UNESCO World Heritage status in 2016.
Iraq's football team won the 2007 AFC Asian Cup.

myths.myth: The numbers 1, 2, 3 were invented in Arabia
myths.fact: They began in India. Arab scholars, including some in Baghdad, carried them to Europe.
No proof has been found at Babylon. Some historians think the gardens stood at Nineveh.
